# Can earlier spreadsheet tasks accelerate synthesis on an independent suite?

## Protocol registered before scoring

Use the pinned CrossBeam conversion of the 89 SyGuS string tasks as the source of experience and its 38 BUSTLE author-designed tasks as the external target. Revision c43cb523fa9887513fb18bf088eb588f3fec5835. File-format inspection revealed that the first SyGuS task repeats training examples in its test field; published test membership alone will not count as transfer. Only use training examples for all SyGuS learning. On each BUSTLE target expose every distinct official training input/output pair. Score only distinct official test inputs absent from that target's training inputs and from any source training input with the same arity. Exclude duplicate support tasks across suites, inconsistent labels on an identical input, and targets with no independent test input or no support; publish exclusions. The evaluator alone reads official target test answers. Never use task names, descriptions, expected programs, tags, test inputs, or test outputs to choose or rank programs. The training observations have been available to prior researchers, so this is a public external pilot.

Use a finite handwritten library over strings: single-column selection; case changes, trimming, character class filters; first/last character, slice and token selection; concatenation of a transformed column with another transformed column separated by common literals; and composition of up to two unary transforms on one column. Freeze a deterministic length-first grammar (enumeration within cost groups fixed in code). No task-specific code, learned constants from held-out examples, neural calls, or external spreadsheet execution. Fit the first support-consistent program on each source task. A program archive then moves those exact program templates to the front in descending source success-count order; the original ordering follows. Compare against the unmodified frozen enumeration and a seeded shuffle of the archived programs' identities among all candidates of the same structural size. Exact programs can move across column names only through shared positional arity. Return the first program matching *all* support examples, or abstain. After selection, score every eligible target regardless of whether our grammar solves it. Report at candidate budgets 64, 512 and exhaustive search. Count candidate programs attempted until stop. Evaluate coverage of any single candidate in the library on all support and test rows as a separate post-hoc oracle. This oracle must never influence the learner.

A feasibility bar before investment is at least five external tasks solvable by the library on all their unique support and held-out examples, and at least one net additional perfectly solved target at 512 candidates for prior-program reuse versus both frozen search and the shuffled control. This project does not assume archived formula transfer will work. Compute the exact total solved and paired wins/losses, and publish task-level outputs. These corpora supply no change history or trustworthy cached downstream dependencies; this pilot can support claims about formula induction and search across independent spreadsheet task sets only.

## Results

**The toy language hit its expressiveness limit on an external suite.** A hindsight oracle exhaustively enumerated the frozen grammar using both support and evaluation answers and could express only **3 of 38** BUSTLE tasks. All 38 qualified for independent evaluation. Two overlapping target test inputs were removed, leaving 273 distinct-within-task held-out examples across the suite. Program reuse cannot repair the 35 cases with no in-language solution.

On the 89 SyGuS source tasks, the enumerator found a support-consistent candidate for 34 and retained 25 distinct program templates. Only support agreement was available as a search signal. At 512 proposals per new target all three search strategies solved the same three tasks on every unseen row. No paired win or loss occurred. At 64 proposals the fixed order solved three and both the learned archive and shuffled archive solved two. The two promotion criteria failed.

| Target with a generalizing solution | Fresh test inputs | Candidates until first fit, fixed | Candidates until first fit, reused |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| First name from second column | 6 | 61 | 72 |
| Last name from first column | 5 | 21 | 8 |
| Remove whitespace and lowercase | 10 | 56 | 62 |

The search order changed where the three usable formulas appeared. A second reverse-order enumeration confirmed the oracle's count. Every reported independent test input was checked against both its local support and all source training inputs. The benchmark developers wrote these tasks; a production-user evaluation would require different data. The combined pilot suggests a concrete requirement for a future program memory: discover new primitives or allow a wider compositional search, then compare with a conventional synthesizer in that same language before attributing a benefit to memory. Extending the grammar after inspecting this suite would turn it into development data.

Run `python3 study.py` locally. It checks the SHA-256 of both input files and fetches the pinned public JSON into the user's cache on first run. No upstream solution programs or descriptions enter search.
